content.value: The spelling suggestion offered for a typed query — "Did you mean …?" — shown for both search engines and the seed of every learned correction.
When a query looks misspelled or returns thin results, Search surfaces a single corrected candidate above the results: *Did you mean
. The suggestion is engine-agnostic — it renders the same whether Postgres Search or the Indx Engine answered the underlying query, and the Web Demo finder shows it as a banner above the result list.

The candidate comes from similarity over the indexed vocabulary — trigram proximity on the Postgres side, the Indx Engine's own fuzzy matching on the other. It is a *display-time* hint: showing it does not change the current results, it only invites a re-query.
The important move happens on acceptance. When a user clicks the suggestion, that click is recorded as feedback in Search Intelligence (the
log). The Auto Correction Loop watches those events; once the same correction is accepted across
rewrites the typo *before* engine dispatch, so
for Postgres Search and the Indx Engine alike — and the suggestion stops being needed.
Suggestion quality and the correction's downstream effect on relevance are tracked by the Golden Eval harness.
